title: Volvo and Waabi launch autonomous freight operations in Texas
key_facts: Volvo Autonomous Solutions (VAS) and Waabi have launched autonomous operations for logistics software company Warp in Texas, the first customer operation in the Volvo-Waabi partnership.
The Volvo VNL Autonomous truck, powered by the Waabi Driver (Waabi's autonomous driving technology), is now carrying freight directly to third-party facilities along the Dallas-Houston corridor.
Warp is described as an open-source freight network offering less-than-truckload (LTL) and full-truckload services to carriers and shippers.
Currently the autonomous hauls are run with an observer in the driver's seat.
The truck is built for autonomy with redundancies for six safety-critical systems.
VAS and Waabi say they will use experience from the Dallas-Houston lane to prepare additional routes and support the wider scaling of autonomous freight in the coming years.

LTL shipping consolidates goods from several customers on tightly coordinated schedules; moving freight directly between facilities without handoffs is said to give LTL providers like Warp a more predictable way to keep networks on schedule.
All statements come from company executives: Nils Jaeger (president, VAS), Lior Ron (COO, Waabi) and Daniel Sokolovsky (CEO, Warp).
